title: OPTIMJACK: When Trusted JavaScript Becomes a Supply Chain Attack
description: On November 16, 2026, attackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into 188 snippets affecting 178 organizations including Zoom, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA and HSBC. The payload replaced cryptocurrency wallet addresses, captured payment card details from first-party forms, collected non-HttpOnly cookies and screenshots, and attempted to deliver exploit kits to iOS devices. Researcher Scott Helme identified the compromise, which lasted approximately 16 hours before cleanup was completed. The attack demonstrated how trusted third-party JavaScript providers can become supply chain attack vectors, bypassing traditional security controls. Organizations with restrictive Content Security Policies blocked some malicious activity, while others remained fully exposed. The incident highlights the need for continuous monitoring of third-party code rather than relying solely on initial vendor assessments.
